_comentario: First Numbers, Part 4 (summer, days 196-260): the English text of each day of Aprendo los números (content/q4.json). Day 198 is the second 'Number names' day (16 and 60, 17 and 70, 18 and 80): see notes/02-english.md.

dias.frase: The holidays are here, and Lucía and Dani count to one hundred with joy.
Lucía packs three books of sixty pages each in her suitcase.
That night, Lucía counts seventy stars from the window.
In the morning they get into the car: the village is eighty kilometres away.
After ninety minutes in the car, Dani falls asleep.
checklist: I can count in tens, up to 100.
I know that 100 is 10 tens.
I can hear the difference between nineteen and ninety.
dias.prompt: Draw the suitcase you would take on holiday.

dias.frase: The car drives into the village, and there are fifty-five pigeons in the square.
Grandma's house has sixty-two flowerpots in the courtyard.
In the courtyard, the lemon tree has fifty-eight lemons.
That night, Lucía listens to the crickets singing, and counts to sixty-six.
On their first day in the village, Dani runs round the square fifty-one times.
checklist: I know the numbers from 51 to 69.
I know which number comes before, and which comes after.
I can read tens and ones.
dias.prompt: Draw Grandma Rosa's house, with its courtyard.

dias.frase: Andrés, who lives next door, has a vegetable garden with seventy-seven tomato plants.
Bigotes, Andrés's cat, has eighty-five orange patches.
Andrés tells Lucía that Bigotes has caught ninety-two flies.
Lucía gives Bigotes some cheese, and Bigotes purrs seventy-four times.
Grandma says there are ninety-nine cats in the village.
checklist: I know the numbers from 71 to 99.
I can read the hundred square.
I can count to 100.

dias.frase: Twelve fish are swimming in the village river.
Lucía gets into the icy water, and fifteen drops splash her.
Dad shows Dani seventeen fish swimming against the current.
Toby gets his paws wet, and leaves fourteen paw prints on the bank.
dias.texto: On the bank there are 8 paw prints from Toby and 6 footprints from Dani. How many prints are there altogether?

dias.frase: In the afternoon, Lucía and Dad see twenty ducks coming down the river.
checklist: I can add up to 20.
I know that 10 + 7 = 17.
I can count on from the bigger number.
dias.prompt: Draw the village river, with its fish.

dias.frase: There are eleven red tomatoes in Grandma's vegetable garden.
Grandma shows Lucía how to pick the ripe tomatoes: thirteen today.
For dinner, they have a salad with nine tomatoes from the garden.
dias.texto: There are 16 tomatoes in the basket, and Grandma puts 7 in the salad. How many are left?

dias.frase: Lucía plants twelve lettuces all by herself, in a row.
Before they leave, Lucía waters her lettuces ten days in a row.
checklist: I can take away up to 20.
I know that 18 − 5 = 13.
I know if a problem is adding or taking away.
dias.prompt: Draw Grandma's vegetable garden, with what you would most like to plant.

dias.frase: The sky turns grey, and eight dark clouds appear.
dias.texto: There are 3 white clouds and 5 grey ones in the sky. How many clouds are there?

dias.frase: A huge clap of thunder makes the windows shake, and Dani counts three flashes of lightning.
dias.texto: Dani sees 7 flashes of lightning, but Lucía only sees 4. How many more does Dani see?

dias.frase: Dad explains that the light arrives before the thunder, and Lucía counts to six.
dias.texto: Lucía counts 9 claps of thunder, and Dani counts 3 fewer. How many does Dani count?

dias.frase: The rain eases off, and eighteen drops are left on the window.
After the storm, there are two wet umbrellas by the door.
checklist: I can listen to a problem.
I can do the calculation, adding or taking away.
I can count how long the thunder takes after the lightning.
dias.prompt: Draw a summer storm, with its lightning.

dias.frase: The family goes to the beach, and Lucía finds five shells.
Dad buys ice creams for everyone: they cost eight euros.
Mum says the sea never stops, and Dani counts ten waves.
Dani builds an enormous sandcastle with twelve buckets of sand.
That night, Lucía writes Sofía a postcard, and sticks one shell on it.
checklist: I know what each coin and each note is worth.
I can count money, up to 20 euros.
I know that two 2-euro coins make 4 euros.
dias.prompt: Draw the beach, with Dani's sandcastle.

dias.frase: The village is having its fiesta, and fifteen lights are hung in the square.
A band plays, and Andrés dances to six songs with Grandma.
At midnight there are fireworks, and Lucía counts twenty.
Afterwards, everyone eats churros: Grandma buys nine.
dias.texto: The churros cost 4 euros, and the hot chocolate costs 5. How much is it altogether?

dias.frase: Dani falls asleep in his chair at two o'clock in the morning.
checklist: I can pay with coins and notes.
I know how much money there is.
I can do a problem with euros.
dias.prompt: Draw the village fiesta, with its lights.

dias.frase: In the square, Dani meets Martín, a boy from the village who is five.
Martín shows Dani where the snails hide: they find seven!
Every afternoon at four, the two boys play under the lemon tree.
Martín invites Dani to his house for tea, at six.
The two friends promise to write each other one letter every week.
checklist: I can tell o'clock times.
I know which hand shows the hour.
I know what time I get up.
dias.prompt: Draw Dani and Martín playing under the lemon tree.

dias.frase: It is the last day of August, and there are three suitcases to pack.
Andrés gives Lucía some honey from his eight beehives.
Grandma hugs them all, and gives each of them ten kisses.
On the way back, Lucía counts eleven red cars.
At last they get home, and Toby runs up and down the hall nine times.
checklist: I can tell half past times.
I know that the long hand pointing down means “half past”.
I know what time I go to bed.
dias.prompt: Draw what you liked best about the summer in the village.

dias.frase: Mum buys Lucía a new school bag, and nine pencils.
They also buy exercise books, and a box of twelve colouring pencils.
Marta sends a letter: the class will have a library with eighty books.
Sofía phones, and they talk for five minutes.
There is only one week to go, and Lucía leaves her school bag by the door.
checklist: I can measure with cubes.
I know which one is longer and which is shorter.
I can pack my school bag.
dias.prompt: Draw your school bag, with what you will take on the first day.

dias.frase: Every afternoon, Lucía and Dani read fourteen pages together.
Dani reads Toby a whole story, thirty-two pages long.
Mum films Dani reading for seven minutes.
Grandma watches the video on the phone, and plays it again: six times!
Dani can read nearly everything now, and Lucía gives him a hundred kisses.
checklist: I can add and take away up to 20.
I can tell the time.
I can count money.
dias.prompt: Draw Dani reading a story to Toby.

dias.frase: The new school year begins, and Lucía puts on her green school bag at nine.
At the school gate, Lucía looks for Sofía among forty children.
Dani reads by himself in class, and his teacher gives him twenty stars.
Lucía counts the workbooks she has filled this year: four!
Before going to sleep, Lucía thinks that this year she has learnt to count to one hundred.
checklist: I know the numbers up to 100.
I can add, take away, count money and tell the time.
I can measure, put in order and compare.
dias.prompt: Draw what you liked best about the whole year.
